feedback.problem:
A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)=\operatorname{tan}⁡t+2t$ meters per second.
Find an expression for the force acting on the body at time $t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{tan}⁡t+2t) \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡t+2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =2\cdot ({sec}^{2}⁡t+2) \\  & =2{sec}^{2}⁡t+4.\end{aligned}
$$
